# Editorial

## Overview

Build readable applications with visible structure and one clear next action per task. Apply this design's declared heading and body families, surfaces and geometry consistently. Prefer meaningful content and neutral separators over decorative panels. The values above describe the selected starting style; the complete scales and roles live in this design's exports.

Use warm paper surfaces, slate ink, square-edged reading panels and understated actions. Prefer long-form content and clear type hierarchy. Use the bundled local fonts and product compositions. Separate page, panel and inset surfaces; keep metadata quiet but readable. Use the exported page/panel/row spacing and title scale consistently, with 44px action targets and brief 160ms interaction feedback. See docs/polish.md for the complete product contract. Available modes: light, dark. Initial mode: light. This file contains exact values for light only.

## Colors

Use purpose-named text, background, button, border and status roles. Keep panels neutral. Use functional color on error/focus/selection states with explicit labels, not decorative card rails. Available modes are declared above; do not invent an unsupported mode. Check contrast in each actual composition; a palette value is not a blanket accessibility approval.

## Typography

Use the declared heading family for headings, body family for reading text and controls, and monospace for code. Start body text at 16px with a 1.5 line-height and normal tracking. Allow headings and labels to wrap. The repository bundles OFL-licensed regular, medium and semibold fonts in assets/fonts; styles/fonts.css loads them locally. Include that stylesheet alongside standalone theme files, or use styles/app.css. Preserve the supplied font licenses. For an independent single-design integration, load shared fonts, library-components.css and base.css, then the selected theme.css; follow that design’s preview.html and docs/designs.md. Avoid squeezing long content into small captions.

## Layout

Use the published website grid: 4 columns at 320–479px, 8 at 480–1023px, and 12 from 1024px. Gutters are 16px on smaller screens and 24px on desktop. Outer margins are 16px, 32px and 64px by range. Console layouts retain 16px gutters/margins. Stack dense regions on narrow screens; use natural scrolling and preserve browser zoom.

Use meaningful semantic HTML for document-based application content, stable resource IDs and DOM-backed editing. Keep efficient specialized runtimes where justified. Token JSON is design interchange, not the default application domain model. Read docs/document-first.md when implementing persistence and editors.

## Elevation & Depth

Favor flat surfaces, whitespace and thin neutral borders. Use small shadows only when they communicate layering. Avoid glossy device frames, continuous ambient motion and gradients that dominate a reading surface. Honor reduced motion while preserving visible loading and status text.

## Shapes

Apply this design's declared card and button radii. Utility icon actions can remain rounded or squared according to purpose. Keep control hit regions at least 44px as a design default, independently of icon size. Do not infer physical size or native dp/sp from CSS pixels.

### Product polish

Use the exported design-page-padding, design-panel-padding, design-row-padding, design-radius-input, design-title-size, design-heading-tracking and design-transition-duration values. The heading size in the metadata is the desktop maximum; use design-title-size-mobile on narrow screens. Use design-text-small for action labels and design-text-caption for supplementary metadata. Follow docs/polish.md and examples/workspace.html for overview, collection/detail and settings compositions. Preserve readable metadata, 44px controls and all error, empty, pending and recovery states.

## Components

Use native buttons for actions and links for navigation. Support default, hover, pressed, focus, disabled and loading states. Keep labels available during pending work. Forms need visible labels, associated hints/errors and current-value serialization. Passwords use native masking; verification codes should support paste and autofill. Group related checkboxes/radios with a legend; use named switches for settings.

Progress must distinguish indeterminate work, actual percent, completion and failure. A local preview or accepted request is not proof of shared persistence or delivery. Preserve dirty work and provide a recovery action after conflicts or failures.

## Do's and Don'ts

- Do use the canonical tokens, public component contracts and meaningful status labels.
- Do make the primary task usable with keyboard, narrow layouts and enlarged text.
- Do show loading, empty, error and recovery states with useful next steps.
- Do retain original design files and add portable exports with explicit conversion limits.
- Do not add decorative northeast arrow icons or colored panel side rails.
- Do not invent backend capabilities, supported imports or verification results.
- Do not include private account metadata, operating procedures or non-Pagelove repository links.


===== docs/designs.md =====

# Selecting and authoring designs

## Selection

Read `designs/catalog.json`, then select the requested ID. With no explicit request, use its `defaultDesign` and `defaultMode`. With an explicit design but no mode, use that design's own `defaultMode`. Never invent a light variant for a dark-only design. The preview falls back to the configured default for an unknown ID, and the selected design's initial mode for an unavailable mode.

Shared guidance describes accessible behavior, document-first development and component contracts. Each design describes visual choices. Selecting Forest should not inherit Classic's white page or serif headings because a root guide was loaded first. Use the selected guide and exports together.

## Sources and generation

`designs/catalog.json` registers IDs and the global default. Each `designs/<id>/design.json` contains its name, description, local default mode, available modes, foundation overrides, appearance and guidance. JSON Schemas are in `schemas/catalog.schema.json` and `schemas/design.schema.json`.

Designs inherit `tokens/foundations.json` and `tokens/semantic.json`. Foundation overrides merge recursively. Each available mode inherits the complete shared semantic map, then applies its role overrides. The build resolves aliases and emits independent, complete formats for every design. Derived files are not separately editable authorities.

Appearance settings connect heading/body families, card/button radius, content width, section spacing and panel shadow to shared CSS. Palettes change actual page/surface colors, controls, links and status roles. A descriptive guide alone does not change running components.

## Default and compatibility

Change the catalog default and rebuild. Root guides, Stitch copy, resolved exports, DTCG files and theme styles follow it. Per-design bundles retain their own defaults. Root exports retain dictionaries keyed by mode, with design/default metadata added. A dark-only default has no `light` entry: consumers must inspect mode availability. Unsupported root DTCG mode files are removed on rebuild.

The original profile JSON is reference-only. Choose `data-design`, not `data-profile`, for a complete design. Existing editorial/invitation profile guides redirect to the supported designs.

## Browser integration

Load `styles/app.css` and put `data-design` plus an available `data-theme` on the HTML element. Omitting both uses the configured default. Typography, geometry, backgrounds and browser control color scheme follow the selection. Nested regions can demonstrate tokens, as the gallery does; whole-document selection is recommended for apps.

For one design, load `styles/fonts.css`, `styles/library-components.css`, `styles/base.css`, then that design's `styles/theme.css`. Add `styles/product.css` if using the product compositions. Do not also load `styles/app.css` or `styles/designs.css`: those are the multi-design entry point. Each generated `designs/<id>/preview.html` demonstrates this independent path, including supported modes, native color scheme and local interactions. Preserve relative font paths and font licenses when copying assets. `styles/base.css` is the shared structure/accessibility layer; theme files supply foundations, semantics and appearance.

The preview uses URL parameters (`?design=forest&mode=dark`), not a hidden saved preference. Changing designs resets to that design's initial mode. Back/forward restores earlier selections. A generated catalog script allows local-file previews without JSON fetches.

## Add a design

1. Create `designs/<id>/design.json`, using an existing definition as a structural starting point. Use a stable lowercase ID and include all appearance settings.
2. Declare supported modes and one local default. Cover page/surface colors, text, actions, focus, disabled/error/selection states and links. Do not use automatic inversion.
3. Write concrete guidance for fonts, colors, shapes and density. Keep font fallbacks and license requirements explicit. Preserve neutral panel borders and no decorative northeast arrows.
4. Register the ID in the catalog. Change the global default only if intended.
5. Build and check. Compare real components in every mode, inspect mobile/keyboard/error/loading states and add a screenshot. Check contrast in actual contexts.

Shared-source changes can affect every design. Exports do not imply verified proprietary native files or live tool imports.

## Product compositions

The complete app preview is examples/workspace.html. It shares the selection contract with the component catalog and adds URL-addressable overview, project and settings screens. Load styles/product.css after styles/app.css for these reusable compositions. New designs must include the product appearance keys listed in schemas/design.schema.json. Read docs/polish.md for the acceptance standard.

Collection links use `collection=fieldnotes`, `collection=ways` or `collection=beginnings` alongside the design/mode/screen parameters. Unknown collections fall back to Fieldnotes. Reading size and motion are local preview preferences and do not redefine the selected design or its export defaults.

All collection previews use examples/selection.js for the same selection rules. Quality and standalone mode selections are URL-backed and restore through browser history. Per-design standalone previews use local defaults, independently of the collection default.

## Portable selection

Each bundle includes tokens/tokens.resolver.json. It combines foundations and composite typography with exactly one supported mode. Multiple-mode bundles expose a mode modifier with the bundle's default; single-mode bundles use unconditional sets and take no mode input. Mode-specific Stitch files are .stitch/light.DESIGN.md and/or .stitch/dark.DESIGN.md. exports/manifest.json identifies release/schema versions and these paths.

Interactive guide links in the gallery, component catalog, workspace, patterns and standalone previews point to the displayed mode's .stitch/MODE.DESIGN.md. The unchanged DESIGN.md entry point still describes that bundle's configured initial mode. Use the mode-specific path when reproducing a selected preview.


===== docs/polish.md =====

# Product polish contract

The same three working app compositions are available in every design at [the workspace preview](../examples/workspace.html): overview, collection/detail and settings. Midnight/dark remains the default. Use the design and mode controls to compare supported combinations. The component catalog remains the reference for individual controls.

## A distinct character, consistent craft

| Design | Direction | Composition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Classic | Precise and professional | Source Serif 4 headings, Inter controls, balanced density and quiet separators |
| Editorial | Warm and literary | Paper surfaces, generous serif titles, longer reading measures and square panels |
| Forest | Grounded and calm | Soft sage surfaces, sans-serif hierarchy, rounded containers and comfortable spacing |
| Midnight | Focused and sophisticated | Plum surfaces, tightly tracked sans-serif titles, compact rows and restrained lavender actions |
| Invitation | Expressive and intimate | Fraunces titles, Inter Tight controls, warm text and generous blue-black compositions |

## Typography and rhythm

Load styles/app.css to include bundled fonts. Standalone theme consumers must also load styles/fonts.css, preserving its relative asset paths. Native consumers must register the supplied fonts with their own platform. Regular, medium and semibold weights are included; italic and other weights use platform synthesis/fallback unless separately supplied. System fallbacks remain intentional during font loading and for missing glyphs. Preserve each OFL license when distributing fonts.

Canonical appearance values export page padding, panel padding, row padding, input radius, title size, heading tracking and interaction duration in every format. Use 16px base body copy, 1.5–1.7 reading line-height, no more than 65 characters in prose measures, and tabular numerals for comparable metrics. Small metadata is supplementary; never use it for essential actions or instructions. Main titles shrink to 36px on narrow screens; controls remain at least 44px high.

## Surfaces and composition

Use the light surface role for the page, regular for panels and strong for inset artwork or progress tracks. Keep borders neutral. Reserve functional color for actions, focus and named states. Avoid wrapping every line in a card: combine open metrics, lists with separators, a single focal project and smaller secondary information. An editorial title treatment replaces stock decoration in the sample project artwork.

styles/product.css provides reusable app shell, navigation, metrics, project panels, activity lists, collections, forms, dialog and status compositions. At narrow sizes the sidebar becomes horizontal navigation, columns stack and all content remains in natural document flow. Avoid fixed content heights and truncated task labels. The product CSS requires app.css and is shared across all selected designs.

## Interaction quality

Actions need default, hover, pressed, focus, disabled and pending states. Use 160ms color/border feedback; no ambient motion. Reduced motion removes transitions and pressed movement. Navigation is URL-addressable, preserves design selection and supports browser history. Search has a useful empty state and clear-search recovery. The create-story dialog supports Escape, native focus containment and return focus. New text uses textContent, never HTML interpolation.

Settings demonstrate required-field and email validation, field-associated errors, first-error focus, saving, completion and reset. The settings demo does not simulate a server: edits and created stories last only until reload. A real application must add persistence, permission failures, conflict recovery and network failure/retry behavior appropriate to its service. Do not imply the preview provides those capabilities.

## Acceptance standard

Inspect every supported design/mode at desktop and 320px widths, including all three screens, loaded fonts, long content, keyboard paths, focus, empty results, invalid submissions, pending/completed actions and reduced-motion behavior. Compare scrollWidth to clientWidth for overflow. Verify contrast for the actual composition. Export checks ensure portable values stay synchronized; they do not certify all accessibility or proprietary tool imports.

## Review refinements

The title size in each generated DESIGN.md and Stitch guide now describes the same maximum title size and tracking used by the app. Mobile titles use design-title-size-mobile. Product content width follows design-content-width; action/label text uses design-text-small and supplementary metadata uses design-text-caption. Decorative artwork labels retain fixed sizes to avoid cropping when reading text is enlarged.

Control boundaries use border-strong and focus uses border-focused. Automated checks cover these roles and error outlines against both page and panel surfaces at a minimum contrast ratio of 3:1; ordinary text checks remain at 4.5:1. This is a targeted check, not blanket accessibility certification.

Collection links carry a collection ID in the URL. Each collection's HTML article owns its items; counts, progress and overview summaries are derived from those articles. Creating an item updates the current collection only. Changing designs or screens preserves local edits until reload. Settings capture submitted values, keep later edits marked unsaved and disable Save only when pending or unchanged. Reset cancels pending work and restores the original preview.

The settings screen offers 100%, 125% and 200% reading sizes and a reduced-motion preference. These apply immediately for preview and reset on reload. Device reduced-motion preferences always take precedence. See [quality checks](../examples/quality.html) for actual font loading at all three supplied weights and effective transition durations. Native browser zoom, screen readers and physical devices require separate testing.


===== docs/foundations.md =====

# Foundations

This guide describes the shared Classic baseline and the original reference profiles. The collection now supplies complete selectable designs: read [selection and authoring](designs.md) and the chosen `designs/<id>/DESIGN.md` first. Design-specific overrides replace the relevant colors, fonts, shape and spacing settings. The old profile references below are historical values, not the active runtime selection mechanism.

## Principles

Make the task readable before adding visual emphasis. Pair editorial headings with precise controls and code. Keep structure visible through spacing, neutral dividers and meaningful labels. Give each task one clear primary next step. Use concrete language and show the state the application actually knows.

Cards and boxes use neutral borders without colored side rails. Functional error/focus/selection outlines on controls are allowed; decorative panel borders are not. Use ordinary action text or meaningful icons instead of decorative northeast arrows.

## Default app library

The canonical foundation contains nine color families: polo blue, purple, olive, old rose, hot pink, neon carrot, cornflower blue, malachite and torch red. Preserve the full scales for flexibility; choose semantic roles for ordinary components. Having a bright raw color does not make it a default background or text color.

Semantic themes cover background, border, button, icon, link and text, in light and dark modes. `--text-regular`, `--background-surface-light`, `--button-strong-default` and similar roles are resolved separately in each theme. Set `data-theme="dark"` or `data-theme="light"` on a document or scoped region. Test contrast in each actual context.

The public library supplies four gradients: purple storm, soft bloom, dawn bloom and sky whisper. Their directions and stop positions are preserved in canonical data. Use gradients selectively for branded emphasis. Keep text on a readable solid surface unless its whole background range has been checked.

## Typography

Display: Source Serif 4, with Georgia/serif fallbacks. The published family stack also names Source Serif Pro; it is retained in foundation exports for fidelity. Body/UI: Inter with platform sans-serif fallbacks. Code: Fira Code with system monospace fallbacks. No network font dependency is needed to read the examples. Bundle separately licensed font files for exact production rendering.

The published font-size scale ranges from 10px to 96px. Font weights are 400, 450 and 500. Text styles combine the foundation family, weight, size, line height and letter spacing. They are reference styles, not blanket approval for 10px body text, tight tracking, or line heights shorter than large display glyphs. The app layer uses 16px body text, a 1.5 line-height, normal body tracking and wrapping labels. Check localization, diacritics and 200% text enlargement.

Spacing uses 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, 48, 64, 80, 96, 112, 128, 144 and 160 CSS pixels. Names such as `space-075` are scale identifiers, not literal pixel values; `--space-075` is 6px.

## Grids

| Website viewport | Columns | Gutter | Outer margin |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 320–479px | 4 | 16px | 16px |
| 480–767px | 8 | 16px | 32px |
| 768–1023px | 8 | 16px | 32px |
| 1024–1512px | 12 | 24px | 64px |
| 1513px and wider | 12 | 24px | 64px |

The console grid retains 16px gutters and margins: 4 columns at 320–479px, 8 at 480–1023px, then 12. Its larger breakpoints are 1024, 1440 and 1768px. These are layout references, not reasons to crop content below 320px. Use readable content measures and allow narrow content to stack.

## Motion

Published defaults: hover 300ms, exit 500ms, skeleton 1s and spin 800ms; standard easing is ease-in-out. Preserve content while status changes and avoid animating every section. The original exit pattern fades and blurs in place before closing the gap; urgent instructions must stay present long enough to read. The recommended app layer disables decorative animation for reduced motion, including the source library's slower-but-continuing spinner. Keep visible loading text when motion stops.

## Optional profiles

Editorial: white, slate ink `#45556C`, Source Serif 4 headings, Inter body and quiet neutral rules. Restrained lavender/olive accents are available. Lighter reference text `#90A1B9` is not approved for body text on white; use the stronger semantic roles or verify an appropriate large-text context.

Invitation: blue-black `#0C0E1A`, navy surfaces, warm off-white `#E8E4DF`, Fraunces headings, Inter Tight body, JetBrains Mono code, with dusty lavender/clay/rose accents. Low-opacity borders are decorative separators, not sufficient boundaries for every control. Check muted text and gradients independently.

The complete Editorial and Invitation designs now map values to shared semantic roles and can be selected with `data-design`. Original `--profile-*` properties remain only for compatibility/reference. Changing `data-profile` alone does not retheme components. Read each complete design's guide for its current palette and geometry.


===== docs/components.md =====

# Component contracts

The [catalog](../examples/catalog.html) is an offline-capable HTML/CSS reference with optional local preview interactions. [components/index.mjs](../components/index.mjs) exports escaped HTML helpers. It does not connect persistence or services. All user-supplied strings are escaped; helpers validate variants and require visible field/choice labels. Load [styles/app.css](../styles/app.css) once.

## Buttons and icon buttons

Use a native button for an action, with an explicit type. Use an anchor with a meaningful destination for navigation. `pl-button` supports strong, regular, light, outlined, outlined-gradient, borderless and borderless-gradient appearances, with lg/md/sm/xs sizes. Icon buttons add `pl-button--icon`; squared buttons add `pl-button--square`.

Represent default, hover, pressed, focus, disabled, loading and skeleton states. Focus must remain visible. Disable a pending action when duplicate activation is invalid and keep an accessible label while its appearance changes. Skeletons are placeholders, not actionable unlabeled controls. Every icon-only action needs an accessible name describing its purpose. The recommended app layer expands small library sizes to at least 44px targets. It does not change the foundation scale.

## Links

Use `pl-link--default` for standalone links and `pl-link--inline` for links in prose. Native underline, visited state, focus and useful link text matter more than decorative icons. Do not make a disabled-looking anchor navigate unexpectedly; if there is no destination, describe availability as text.

## Fields: basic, password and phone

Use `pl-field` with a visible label, `pl-field__control`, `pl-field__input` and an optional `pl-field__hint`. Labels reference a stable unique input ID. Associate hints and errors with `aria-describedby`; set `aria-invalid="true"` for an invalid value. Do not substitute placeholder text for a label. Keep a value when validation fails and explain the correction.

Use native input types and appropriate autocomplete/inputmode. Password fields use the browser's `type="password"` rather than a second string masked with asterisks; changing visibility keeps the same underlying value. The catalog provides a named visibility button with pressed state. Do not log or store passwords in a component demo. Phone input accepts an international number; a country selector is optional and must not silently reinterpret stored data. Actual phone verification requires a separate service contract.

## Verification codes and segmented PIN

The source library includes segmented PIN cells, 4–8 digits, with empty/incorrect error feedback. This repository recommends one native input with numeric input mode, one-time-code autocomplete and a visible digit-count hint. It preserves paste, autofill and a single accessible name without custom key movement. This is an intentional adaptation, not a claim to reproduce the original segmented interaction.

If implementing segmented cells, define paste distribution, backspace, selection, focus order, error clearing and current-value serialization. Keep an equivalent accessible single-field route. A component only collects a code; it does not establish its validity or security.

## Checkbox, radio and switch

Use native checkboxes for independent selections; a group can use a fieldset and legend. Use same-name native radio buttons for exclusive selections, with one group legend. A switch uses a native checkbox with `role="switch"` for a labeled setting; state must remain available to assistive technology. Labels form part of the target.

The library supports left/right labels and top-aligned switch labels, plus disabled/loading/skeleton appearances. A loading appearance alone must not leave an action repeatable when the operation needs duplicate protection. Native states and application acceptance remain distinct. Keep skeleton labels present or provide a named loading region rather than interactive placeholders.

## Progress indicators

Indeterminate progress has a name and no invented percentage. Determinate progress has bounds and an actual value. The source library includes radial sizes xxs/xs/sm/md/lg/xl (16/24/32/40/48/56px) and progress/done/error presentations. Adjacent visible text must explain completion or failure and the available next action.

The helper provides a radial determinate indicator; the catalog also demonstrates native `progress`. Clamp numeric values to the supported range and reject non-finite values. Progress reaching 100% is evidence only for the measured operation, not proof of external delivery. Reduced-motion mode stops decorative spin while preserving the loading label.

The size option applies to both determinate and indeterminate helpers: xxs/xs/sm/md/lg/xl correspond to 16/24/32/40/48/56 CSS pixels. Icon-only pending buttons include the original action and an in-progress indication in their accessible name.

## Integration limits

Checkbox helper markup includes both check and mixed-state glyphs; set the native input's indeterminate property for a partial selection. Keep the glyph container hidden from assistive technology because the native input owns the state. The app layer lets long choice labels wrap, keeps control graphics from shrinking, and uses native checkbox/radio/switch rendering in forced colors. Keep styles/base.css after the preserved source-library stylesheet.

React, Vue and Svelte files are small usage examples, not compiled framework packages. Native Swift/Kotlin outputs are dictionaries of CSS strings, not platform colors, dp/sp or SwiftUI views. The library's CSS is preserved separately; the recommended app layer makes documented readability, target-size, native-input and reduced-motion adaptations. Consult [the source inventory](../reference/library-inventory.json) for every observed public story and variant.

Pending button helpers and framework examples preserve the supplied action label and append an in-progress indication. Skeleton helper buttons remain disabled and retain an explicit accessible name even when their visual text is hidden. Framework examples still require compilation and integration tests in the consuming application.

## Reusable interaction patterns

components/patterns.mjs exports select, textarea, notice, disclosure, breadcrumbs, tabs, confirmation, errorSummary, enhancePatterns and openConfirmation. Import it as a JavaScript module over HTTP; load styles/patterns.css after the selected theme. All content arguments are plain text and escaped. IDs must be unique within the consuming document. Breadcrumb URLs accept HTTP or relative destinations and reject executable schemes.

Tabs require a nonempty items array of label/text objects and use immediate activation; do not use them for slow network-loaded panels without changing the activation contract. Call enhancePatterns once on a mounted root and retain its cleanup function. Confirmation uses native dialog: openConfirmation(dialog, trigger) restores focus on close; the safe Cancel action has initial focus. Use disclosure for supplementary content, never to hide required instructions. Notice supports polite status and urgent alerts; avoid nested live regions in consuming apps.

The patterns fixture demonstrates a captioned sortable table and bounded pagination using DOM-backed records, plus a complete form-error summary and recovery flow. These compositions can be copied and adapted; they are not a server-backed grid API. Every helper and composition remains Preview until the documented browser/AT acceptance matrix is complete.

Pattern styling is opt-in: helpers emit ds-select, ds-textarea, ds-dialog and data-ds-tabs hooks. Tables use ds-table inside ds-table-scroll, with ds-table-controls for pagination. Unrelated tables, dialogs and tab widgets retain their styling and event handling. enhancePatterns acts only on its own tab groups inside the supplied root. Keep the returned cleanup function when unmounting. Button corners, input corners, panel padding and section gaps use the selected design's separate appearance values.

openConfirmation wraps Tab and Shift+Tab between the dialog's visible, enabled controls, preserves native Escape, resets prior results and returns focus to the opener on close. Its key handler is removed on close. Controls hidden by CSS, disabled or inside an inert region are omitted from the loop; browser shortcuts and already-handled widget keys are preserved.

The patterns preview has design/mode controls with URL/history state. Switching design preserves form content; reloading resets the local example. Its design-guide link points to the exact mode. Text-spacing stress rules live only in the preview stylesheet, not in the reusable component styles.


===== docs/document-first.md =====

# Document-first development for applications

Adapted from Pagelove, *Document-first development for websites and applications*, edition 2.4 (2026). Changes: condensed and reorganized for a public design system; platform-specific evidence, operations, private examples and internal references omitted. This adaptation is CC BY 4.0: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/. Distributed source: https://github.com/pagelove/design-system/blob/main/docs/document-first.md.

## Model the information before the interface

Identify the entities, relationships and operations that matter to the user. Prefer semantic HTML for document-based domain information and the live DOM as its editable client working model. Make meaningful resources independently understandable and addressable through stable IDs or URLs. Addressability does not imply public access.

An article, catalog record, workflow item, scene or quest can be a bounded document resource. A document is not a requirement to create one file per object or use a specific database. Transactions, binary assets, simulation buffers and established external systems can retain more suitable representations.

## Declare authority

For every value, identify whether it is authoritative, derived, cached, a local draft, pending confirmation, accepted or historical. Name the owner, schema/version, allowed operations and persistence boundary. Do not keep independently editable HTML and JSON copies of the same domain fields. Derived views must be rebuildable from their declared source.

This repository's JSON token files are a justified design-tool interchange format. They describe design values rather than replacing document-based app content. JSON transport envelopes, receipts and revision metadata likewise do not create another editable domain authority.

Choose aggregate boundaries that support the required consistency. Shared constraints across several records need a transaction, enforced operation or explicit recovery policy that actually provides the promised guarantee.

## Separate meaning, appearance and behavior

Use headings, lists, tables, articles, forms and native controls to express meaning. Apply visual styles through tokens and CSS. Attach behavior through named commands, scoped bindings and documented events/results. Keep temporary menus, focus state and selection overlays outside persisted content unless they are deliberate domain values.

An editor is a view over the model. Identify its source resource and exact editable root. Read the current form-control properties when serializing: HTML attributes and `outerHTML` alone do not necessarily contain the current input, checkbox or selection values. Validate bounded values and preserve allowed nested structure. Do not replace a complete resource with a partial extracted fragment.

Composed views must retain provenance: identify their source and supported mutation target. If origin or permission is ambiguous, keep the view read-only. Check actual platform capabilities before relying on routing, composition, subscriptions or declarative schemas.

## Enforce writes where they become durable

Client-side constraints improve experience but do not establish authorization, uniqueness or trusted shared results. Establish which actual read/write path checks actor permissions, shape, ownership, references and invariants. A trusted authoring endpoint can have a different contract from an application mutation endpoint.

For concurrency, use supported atomic conditional writes, revision checks or a suitable transaction. On a conflict, keep the user's draft and explain compare/reload/reapply choices. Do not silently overwrite current accepted data or retry a consequential action with an unknown outcome.

Freeze a pending command's identity and payload while it is in flight. Retrying the same intent should follow a declared duplicate/receipt policy. Distinguish a local save, queued request, server acceptance and external delivery. A timeout is not proof of failure or success; reconcile against supported receipts before resubmitting an irreversible operation.

## Design recovery

Define behavior for refresh, back/forward navigation, account changes, loss of connectivity, stale revisions and interrupted writes. Scope local storage/queues to the actor and resource. Preserve unsent work; clearly label offline drafts. Incoming changes must not silently overwrite dirty work or trigger an outgoing save loop. Specify subscription gaps, reset and reconnection behavior.

Release code separately from user-managed content. Version stored formats, define compatibility and validate before switching readers. Test restoration or forward repair for consequential changes. A backup is not verified until an isolated restore succeeds.

## Keep the experience usable

Provide a useful reading experience without unnecessary JavaScript. Preserve native controls, keyboard paths, visible focus, field errors and status. Show data freshness when it affects decisions. Explain empty, loading, partial, stale, denied and failed states with a useful next action.

Measure the workload before choosing an optimization: document size, network, layout, painting, query work, simulation and graphics can have different bottlenecks. Keep efficient specialized runtimes where appropriate; avoid forcing every transient value into the DOM. Use summaries, pagination and bounded work when they improve the actual task.

## Apply the guide proportionately

1. Scope the feature and select its application profile.
2. Choose the HTML/DOM default or record a concrete representation exception.
3. Define resources, stable IDs, authority, formats and supported operations.
4. Establish actual enforcement with a valid case and a case that must be rejected.
5. Implement the scoped view/editor and explicit behavior.
6. Handle applicable drafts, conflicts, retries, incoming changes and recovery.
7. Verify exact operation paths separately from browser task behavior.
8. Report changes, evidence, exceptions and remaining gaps.

## Application profiles

| Profile | Additional focus |
| --- | --- |
| Publishing and documentation | Readable semantic content, navigation, metadata, progressive enhancement |
| Catalogs and directories | Stable record IDs, filtering, useful no-results, source provenance |
| Analytics and dashboards | Units, aggregation windows, freshness, accessible table alternatives |
| Workflows and transactions | Permissions, bounded operations, concurrency, receipts and recovery |
| Editors and creative tools | Scoped bindings, draft safety, undo, import validation and round-trip fidelity |
| Games and simulations | Authored content vs runtime state, responsive controls, checkpoints and bounded rendering |

## Exception record

Record the requirement, why HTML/DOM is unsuitable, owner, authoritative representation, derivation/reference relationship, validation and recovery. Required external JSON integration or specialized simulation buffers can justify an exception. A preference for duplicating editable data does not establish one.

## Evidence and completion

Maintain a compact record of the changed revision, environment, operation, actor, expected result, actual result and limitation. Check validation, rejection, concurrency and restoration where applicable. Separately inspect keyboard tasks, responsive layout, control prefill/current values and browser recovery. Mark each applicable check pass, fail, pending or not applicable with a reason. A local fixture does not prove deployment behavior, and a screenshot does not prove an entire task.


===== docs/games.md =====

# Game and simulation experience

Adapted from Pagelove contributors, *Web Game Development Handbook*, edition 2.14.0 (2026), MIT licensed. This public summary selects reusable interaction, architecture, performance and recovery guidance; project-specific integrations and operational references are omitted. See LICENSE.

## First playable experience

State the player's goal, controls and win/loss conditions before play. Start with a complete small journey: start, act, understand feedback, pause, resume, reach a result and retry or continue. Make the next action clear. Give immediate visible feedback; optional music, effects and haptics supplement it. Do not claim that passing technical checks establishes enjoyment.

Introduce mechanics through a short safe first action or optional help. Returning players should be able to find controls again without replaying a long tutorial. Keep score, completion and earned rewards distinct. Describe which result is local and which is accepted by a shared service.

## State and content

Separate authored levels/rules, runtime simulation, rendered output, player preferences and durable progress. Prefer semantic HTML for document-based authored content and DOM-backed editing. Use a specialized runtime representation for simulation where justified; preserve stable source identity and a declared rebuild/conversion path.

Keep test play separate from authoring. A test run should not silently publish a level, consume real inventory or submit a ranked score. Validate imported content before applying it atomically. Undo and checkpoints must refer to compatible rules/content versions. Define what a checkpoint includes and whether restore is all-or-nothing.

## Input and mobile layout

Use native DOM controls for menus, help and settings. Map keyboard, pointer and touch to the same validated actions. Provide selection/action alternatives to required dragging and avoid hover-only information. For ordinary discrete actions, activate once on click/release. Continuous held actions need explicit ownership and cancellation.

Track independent contacts by pointer ID when simultaneous actions are needed. Handle release, pointer cancellation, lost capture, focus loss, hidden pages, dialogs and removed controls. Cleanup must be idempotent; releasing one input source must not cancel another source's still-held action. Require fresh input after interruption when appropriate.

At the normal adopted scale, fit a bounded playfield, essential status and primary controls together so ordinary mobile play does not require page scrolling. Allow natural scrolling for help, forms and enlarged-text fallback. Do not disable browser zoom to meet the fit target. Account for safe-area insets, browser chrome, orientation and virtual keyboards. Resizing should not accidentally change physics or competitive field of view.

Frequent targets start at 44×44 CSS pixels; 48px targets with 8–12px separation can be useful for play controls. These are project defaults rather than universal web requirements. Separate restart, purchase and destructive actions from rapid play. Avoid global gesture suppression; scope any exclusive manipulation region narrowly.

## Feedback, accessibility and audio

Show selected, pressed, unavailable, cooldown, pending and rejected states with visible meaning. Preserve readable text and focus outside the playfield. Supply appropriate alternatives for motion, flashing, audio cues and time pressure. Keep essential help reachable while paused.

Audio starts through supported user activation and has separate music/effects controls when useful. Handle muted/denied playback without blocking progress. Bound active voices, decode work, loops and resource ownership. Pause or adapt audio when the document is hidden according to the declared game policy; never promise to pause an authoritative multiplayer world just because one client hides.

## Performance and resilience

Profile representative play before optimizing. Separate CPU simulation, layout, drawing, GPU work, compositing, asset loading and memory costs. Set frame/input/memory budgets for the supported environment, measure sustained play and cold effects, and record the measurement boundary. Device-pixel-ratio caps, batching, caching, lower effect quality and workers are conditional optimizations, not default requirements.

Keep render data derived. Dispose observers, listeners, timers, textures, buffers and audio nodes at clear lifecycle boundaries. A graphics-context loss or optional API failure needs a visible recovery path. Preserve meaningful progress through refresh/back/history return according to the game's save contract. Never label a local score as verified shared acceptance.

## Genre-specific emphasis

| Category | Essential checks |
| --- | --- |
| Arcade/action | Timing, collision clarity, independent inputs and fast retry |
| Platform/exploration | Camera, movement feedback, readable hazards and checkpoint restore |
| Puzzle/procedural | Solvability, deterministic seeds, hint policy and undo |
| Card/board/turn-based | Legal actions, turn ownership, hidden information and exact scoring |
| Narrative | Reading pace, branch persistence, accessible choices and localization |
| Rhythm | Declared timing/calibration, audio lifecycle and non-audio feedback |
| Asynchronous multiplayer | Versioned rules, duplicate commands, receipts and calendar/timezone boundaries |
| Real-time multiplayer | Server authority, disconnect behavior, reconciliation and bounded latency claims |

## Acceptance walkthrough

Test start/play/pause/resume/result/retry, then refresh or history return at meaningful points. Inspect portrait/landscape, short-height windows, keyboard-only operation, enlarged text, slow/offline behavior and optional audio/fullscreen denial. Real browser input establishes more than synthetic event dispatch, but desktop emulation does not prove actual phone behavior. Keep unsupported environment claims explicit.


===== docs/accessibility.md =====

# Accessibility and responsive behavior

Target WCAG 2.2 AA for the consuming application and evaluate complete tasks. This repository supplies patterns; it does not certify applications built from them. The standard is available at https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/.

- Text generally needs 4.5:1 contrast; qualifying large text needs 3:1. Check actual backgrounds, alpha blending, gradients and every theme. Meaningful control boundaries and visual states need applicable non-text contrast. Decorative separators are a different case.
- Preserve semantic landmarks and heading order. Label fields and groups, name icon buttons, describe meaningful images, and hide decorative graphics from assistive technology.
- All actions need a keyboard path with visible focus. Dialogs require an appropriate focus lifecycle and escape/recovery behavior. Do not hide essential actions behind hover or a gesture alone.
- Associate errors with fields and describe a correction. Announce meaningful asynchronous status without making every progress tick a disruptive alert. Do not use color alone for status or selection.
- Use 44px targets as this design system's default for frequent controls. WCAG 2.2 AA's target-size criterion uses 24px with exceptions; the 44px criterion is AAA with its own exceptions. Design defaults and conformance rules are distinct.
- Reflow at 320 CSS pixels, preserve zoom and inspect 200% text enlargement. Tables or inherently two-dimensional content can have a deliberate scroll region with context; ordinary form controls and essential actions must remain reachable.
- Allow wrapping and long translated/RTL text. Use logical properties when practical. Do not rely on a font family declaration to guarantee that a particular font loaded.
- Honor reduced motion; keep visible feedback when animations stop. Avoid flashing and unnecessary autoplay. Audio needs a useful independent control and a non-audio path to essential meaning.
- Check browser contrast modes, pointer/keyboard switching, virtual keyboard occlusion and safe-area clearance. Desktop emulation is useful but does not prove physical-device behavior.

Run automated checks where available, then inspect the actual task separately. Record build, environment, input path, result and limits. Missing screen-reader or device evidence stays pending rather than becoming a pass.

The app layer imports styles/forced-colors.css, generated from the shared semantic role names. In forced colors, it maps text, surfaces, links, controls and focus to system colors instead of retaining a dark theme's pale text on a forced light canvas. Native choice controls retain their state; explicit contrast assertions complement screenshot review. Preserve this relative stylesheet import when copying base.css.

## Executable acceptance fixtures

Serve examples/patterns.html and select design/mode through URL parameters. dir=rtl, spacing=expanded and size=200 combine layout stress cases; they are fixtures, not proof of browser zoom support. The expanded spacing fixture uses 1.5 line height, 2em paragraph spacing, .12em tracking and .16em word spacing. Tests exercise keyboard tabs, confirmation cancellation/focus return, error-summary recovery, pagination boundaries and axe checks. See docs/support.md for mandatory manual checks and untested environments.


===== docs/patterns.md =====

# Application patterns

## Settings and forms

Present related settings in named groups with visible labels. Choose whether changes apply immediately or on Save, and explain that behavior. Keep pending, accepted and rejected state distinct. Preserve dirty work on a failed request. For shared state, handle a changed revision explicitly rather than overwriting newer data.

## Collections and detail views

Use stable IDs and meaningful item names. Keep filters, counts and empty/no-results explanations connected. Preserve context when moving into a detail view and back. Distinguish no matching items, no permission and an unavailable source. A read-only detail page can still expose useful source/freshness information.

## Editors

Keep the authored resource separate from preview UI and temporary tools. Use semantic HTML/DOM-backed editing for document-based information. Validate imports before replacement, preserve complete structure on round trips, and define undo, drafts and version compatibility. A preview or test run must not silently publish work.

## Dashboards and reports

Show units, relevant time windows and source freshness. Provide text/table equivalents for meaningful charts. A status should reflect the evidence actually known, with an explicit unknown state when appropriate. Do not make decorative metrics look like verified business outcomes.

## Editorial pages

Use a minimal header, readable serif heading, short explanation, concrete evidence and one primary next step. Vary narrative, code, diagrams and comparisons instead of repeating an identical card grid. A light editorial profile and a dark invitation profile are available without forcing every app to use a marketing layout.

## Presentations and reading views

For an HTML deck, 1280×720 with roughly 72px side clearance is a starting canvas. Use approximately 50px headings, 72px cover titles, 27px body and 23px short code examples; verify at actual scaled viewing size. Reduce content instead of shrinking everything. Provide a semantic reading view that reflows without depending on presenter JavaScript. Notes and presenter tooling are separate from the audience content.

## Sharing and handoff

Explain the output's destination and actual save/share state. Provide meaningful page titles and descriptions, responsive imagery and alternative text. Retain source and license notices. Treat a copied link, saved local draft, service acceptance and final delivery as distinct outcomes.


===== docs/formats.md =====

# Formats and conversion contracts

Shared foundation/semantic JSON, designs/catalog.json and each designs/<id>/design.json are the editable design values. `npm run build` generates the full set of formats under every design, with default-compatible copies at the repository root. Component source and guidance remain authored files. An adapter must identify its source and limitations; never maintain competing manually edited exports. Modes follow each design's declaration; do not assume every bundle has a light entry.

## Supported representations

- Markdown and plain text: human/agent guidance and context bundles. README and AGENTS.md are entry points. `llms.txt` is an optional documentation index, not a guaranteed ingestion mechanism.
- JSON: canonical design interchange and resolved exports. This is a design-tool requirement, not a new default for application domain data.
- JSON Schema: `schemas/semantic.schema.json` describes the semantic source's shape and alias syntax using draft 2020-12. Alias resolution is separately checked by the build. Other interchange outputs do not claim this schema applies to them.
- DTCG 2025.10: typed color, dimension, number, font, duration, cubic-bezier, gradient and shadow values. Load a design's `foundations.tokens.json` plus exactly one of its available mode files. Appearance aliases inherit the target type. Transition durations use duration objects; relative tracking uses numbers with CSS extensions. No-shadow is represented as a transparent zero-size shadow, with the original CSS none preserved in extensions. Unsupported CSS conversions stop the build instead of inventing a DTCG type. Modes are separate files rather than an invented DTCG theme field. Specification: https://www.designtokens.org/TR/2025.10/format/.
- DTCG extension: gradient direction and original CSS strings live under `com.pagelove.design-system` extensions. Relative letter-spacing in em is represented as a number with the original CSS retained; DTCG dimensions use px/rem. Consumers must honor that documented conversion rather than interpreting the number as pixels. Individual properties remain available; tokens/typography.tokens.json adds named composite text styles. Relative tracking is converted to a dimension at that style’s font size; line height becomes a ratio.
- Tokens Studio JSON: global foundation set plus the design's available semantic modes. Enable global and one available mode at a time. Dimensions, font properties, radii and composite typography have supported Tokens Studio types; gradients use color values. CSS-only motion and shadow-none properties remain other. Font stacks reduce to the first family. No plugin import has been claimed tested.
- YAML, XML and CSV: portable structured views. XML is a repository interchange schema, not an Android resource file. YAML scalars are quoted to preserve leading-zero scale IDs and CSS strings.
- CSS, Sass and Less: CSS supplies runtime theme aliases; Sass contains resolved theme maps and Less contains configured-default aliases and explicit mode-prefixed string variables. Native CSS custom properties remain the preferred browser runtime.
- ES module, CommonJS and TypeScript: resolved theme dictionaries; no UI framework dependency. TypeScript adds literal keys/types.
- Swift and Kotlin: portable dictionaries of CSS strings. Parse CSS colors and deliberately map px/rem/em/seconds/fonts to native conventions. These do not pretend CSS pixels are dp, sp, iOS points or physical pixels. Gradients and easing require explicit native adapters.
- HTML and SVG: semantic component examples and inspectable vector palette. Preview screenshots, when present, are supplemental visual evidence and never the editable token source.
- Stitch DESIGN.md: structured YAML values plus descriptive Markdown. The root and `.stitch` copies are generated from the same design template; each selectable design has its own generated guide. No private project IDs or live account metadata are distributed.
- React TSX, Vue SFC and Svelte: small button integration examples. Compile them in the consuming framework/version; they are source examples, not installed framework packages.

## Adding more formats

Preserve originals when supplied, document licensing/provenance and provide portable exports where useful. Do not rename JSON to `.fig`, `.sketch` or another proprietary extension and claim native compatibility. Add a generation path, a bounded validation check and an explicit loss/limitation note for every new adapter.

File readability does not guarantee automatic discovery or accurate visual interpretation. Supply a short entry point, relevant examples and explicit values. Keep guidance concise enough to load by task rather than requiring an entire repository in one context window.

## Consumer checks

Typography overrides support positive px/rem font sizes; px/rem/em tracking or unitless zero; and nonnegative unitless/em line-height multipliers or px/rem line heights. DTCG composites preserve px/rem tracking and convert em tracking using the associated font size. Line height is a ratio; mixed px/rem ratios assume a 16px root. Tokens Studio preserves absolute tracking/line heights and converts em tracking or multiplier line heights to percentages. Unsupported units fail generation instead of producing guessed values. These mappings follow [DTCG typography](https://www.designtokens.org/TR/2025.10/format/#typography), [Tokens Studio letter spacing](https://docs.tokens.studio/manage-tokens/token-types/typography/letter-spacing) and [line height](https://docs.tokens.studio/manage-tokens/token-types/typography/line-height). Live application in the target tools remains unverified.

Dark-only resolver bundles use unconditional sets rather than a one-context modifier, following the [DTCG contexts recommendation](https://www.designtokens.org/TR/2025.10/resolver/#contexts). Supply no modifier input to those bundles. Classic, Editorial and Forest expose a mode modifier with light/dark contexts. The repository consumer follows the declared references and resolution order, rejects unsupported inputs and cycles, and checks output parity; it supports the emitted subset, not arbitrary resolver documents.

The checks execute the ES module and CommonJS exports, parse CSV, and compare all values with the resolved canonical dictionaries for the root and each design. DTCG checks reject unknown emitted types, invalid units, mismatched aliases and malformed supported values. These are stricter repository contract checks, not independent full-spec certification or live proprietary-tool import tests.

Generated additions: per-design DTCG resolver, mode-specific Stitch guides, release manifest and Tailwind v4 @theme inline CSS. Live Figma/Stitch imports remain pending; official Stitch lint is a separate automated check. XML schema-version is 1; release-version tracks package.json.


===== docs/support.md =====

# Support and verification contract

Version 0.5.1 retains Midnight/dark as the collection default. This is a source collection, not an installed framework component library.

| Surface | Maturity | Evidence and boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Five designs / eight modes, CSS and resolved JSON | Supported source contract | Deterministic generation, alias/value checks, selected contrast pairs |
| DTCG tokens and per-design resolver | Preview adapter | Typed values, typography composites, reference-driven composition and mode checks; dark-only bundles use sets; not full-spec certification |
| Tokens Studio | Preview adapter | Typed values and composite typography generated; live Figma application remains pending |
| Stitch guides | Preview adapter | Pinned official linter; exact role parity per mode; live Stitch import remains pending |
| Tailwind v4 | Preview adapter | Generated theme mapping; compile smoke check; load design theme before adapter |
| HTML helpers and patterns | Preview components | Escaping, semantics and task fixtures; no persistence or service integration |
| React/Vue/Svelte snippets | Illustrative only | Not compiled packages |
| Swift/Kotlin dictionaries | Interchange only | CSS strings, not native UI values |

## Browser and accessibility acceptance

CI targets pinned Playwright Chromium, Firefox and WebKit in a digest-pinned Ubuntu Noble container matching the Playwright package version. Update both pins together. This follows the [official CI container guidance](https://playwright.dev/docs/ci#via-containers) and avoids downloading system dependencies on each run. These are test engines, not a promise that every historical browser release works. Real Safari/iOS, Android, NVDA and VoiceOver results must be recorded separately. Latest test artifacts and reference/CORE-CONTROLS-REVIEW.md give actual results; configured tests are not evidence that a run passed.

Every new component must cover visible labels, keyboard path, focus, disabled/pending/error/empty states where relevant, and safe insertion of text. For dialogs: initial focus, containment, Escape, and return focus. For tabs: arrow/Home/End keys, selected state and linked panels. For forms: error summary focus, associated inline errors, retained values and recovery. For tables: captions, column semantics, sort state, pagination boundaries and named scrolling regions.

Required environment checks: 320/768/1440 CSS px; 200% text; WCAG text-spacing overrides; RTL/mixed-direction text; reduced motion; forced colors; actual zoom; virtual keyboard occlusion; NVDA/Firefox and VoiceOver/Safari tasks. Automation covers a subset, and never substitutes for the latter manual checks. Results are pass/fail/untested, with build, browser/AT version, operating system, action and evidence.

The original helper fixture at tests/fixtures/core-controls.html exercises checkbox checked/mixed states, native radio/switch keyboard paths, disabled choices, icon-only pending names, all six determinate progress sizes, RTL/enlarged-text reflow and native forced-color fallbacks. Tests also verify selected-mode guide links across catalog, workspace, gallery and standalone previews. These extend automated coverage without replacing manual acceptance.

## Live import acceptance procedure

1. Record the target tool/version and the design/mode. Use an empty disposable document.
2. For Tokens Studio, import exports/tokens-studio.json, enable global plus one mode, and apply dimensions, radius, fonts and colors to a panel, button and text. Check resolved values, not just token presence. The font family adapter uses the first family; CSS preserves fallbacks. CSS-only properties remain explicitly typed other.
3. For Stitch, import .stitch/MODE.DESIGN.md, request the same panel/button/form, and compare surfaces, text, typography, shape and component states. Repeat all eight combinations. Do not infer support from lint success.
4. Save a public-safe screenshot, observed differences and a result. Failed or missing evidence keeps the adapter in Preview status.

No account connections for these live imports are configured in this checkout's automated workflow. Contributors can supply results using this procedure.

## Performance budgets

The WOFF2 archive must stay under 2 MB, the collection theme CSS under 250 KB and gallery HTML under 30 KB. These are build-size guards, not network timing guarantees. The current 18 WOFF2 fonts total approximately 1.24 MB; only used faces are normally fetched. Preserve TTF originals and all OFL notices. Do not preload every face.

Before hosting, measure cold-cache gallery and workspace loads on a representative mobile connection: font bytes fetched, LCP, CLS, image transfer and responsiveness. Investigate regressions against the previous release. Real network/physical-device measurements remain a separate acceptance task.

## Release and migration

Package releaseVersion identifies the shipped collection. Catalog/schemaVersion identifies an interchange contract; XML explicitly separates schema-version and release-version. Until 1.0, breaking public token, selector or helper changes require a minor release, migration notes and before/after examples. Compatible fixes use a patch release.

Avoid silent removals: introduce replacement aliases, mark deprecation in documentation, retain them for at least one subsequent minor release and document removal. Changing the default is an intentional consumer-visible change, never an incidental build consequence. Promote an adapter from Preview only after its consumer checks and live import evidence exist.

See docs/releases.md for changes and CONTRIBUTING.md for contribution requirements.

Visual regression compares the eight desktop pattern states in each of three pinned Linux browser engines against tests/visual. It allows at most 0.2% differing pixels for rendering noise. Baselines are not refreshed automatically; inspect changes before replacing them. Local non-Linux runs annotate that pixel comparison is not run, while retaining task checks. Mobile/RTL/forced-color captures remain review artifacts rather than pixel baselines.


===== docs/content.md =====

# Content and recovery

Use the same voice across designs: direct, respectful and specific. Visual character changes; the meaning of an action does not. Use sentence case. Name actions with a verb and object. Keep essential instructions visible; a tooltip is supplementary.

| Situation | Pattern | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Empty collection | Explain what belongs here and offer the first action | No projects yet. Create a project. |
| No search results | Repeat the scope and offer recovery | No projects match this search. Clear search. |
| Invalid input | Identify the field and correction; preserve the input | Enter an email address in the format name@example.com. |
| Network failure | State what failed, what was retained and a safe next step | Your changes could not be saved. Your draft is still here. Try again. |
| Pending action | Keep the action recognizable; avoid invented duration | Saving description… |
| Destructive action | Name the affected item and consequence; prefer the safe initial focus | Delete this draft? This cannot be undone. |
| Permission failure | Distinguish lack of access from absent data | You do not have access to this project. Contact its owner. |
| Local demonstration | State the persistence boundary | Saved in this preview. Reloading resets it. |

Do not announce routine changes repeatedly. Use a polite status region for asynchronous outcomes; reserve alerts for urgent errors. Include units and time zones where ambiguity affects a decision. Use locale formatting and plural rules rather than concatenated English strings. Avoid truncating the only available name for a resource.

## Charts and new compositions

UI success/error colors are not a categorical chart palette. For a chart-specific extension, define categorical and sequential roles per supported mode, labels/patterns as alternatives to color, a text/table equivalent and explicit unknown/missing-data states. Validate the chart in its actual context before adding those roles to the canonical source.

The shared Studio fixture intentionally isolates theme differences. Add an editorial reader, dense table or mobile workflow only with a concrete task and acceptance evidence. Do not invent native adapters or additional color schemes merely to increase format counts.
